newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Metals cuts Pillara lead/zinc ore.
newsitem.headline: Western Metals cuts Pillara lead/zinc ore.

text.p: Lead and zinc producer Western Metals Ltd said on Thursday that it had reduced its resource and reserve estimates for the Pillara, formerly Blendevale, project in Western Australia after completing a A$20 million underground feasibility and drilling programme.
The company said the inferred and indicated resource at June 30 stood at 18.05 million tonnes, based on zinc cut-off grade of three percent, grading 7.6 percent zinc and 2.4 percent lead.
It said the resource at December 31 last year, with the same cut-off, was 22.1 million tonnes grading 7.2 percent zinc and 2.2 percent lead.

The reserve estimate, based on a five percent cut-off, had been cut to 10.55 million tonnes grading 8.1 percent zinc and 2.5 percent lead from an end-December estimate of 14.86 million tonnes grading 7.5 percent zinc and 2.4 percent lead.
The company has previously said the mine would be commissioned on schedule in mid-1998.

It also said the Kapok deposit in Western Australia had a total resource of 4.096 million tonnes at June 30, with a five percent zinc cut-off, grading 9.1 percent zinc and 7.1 percent lead. Kapok began mining operations in the latest quarter.
Total reserves stood at 2.629 million tonnes grading 8.4 percent zinc and 6.7 percent lead.

Western Metals said its Cadjebut mill produced a record 28,954 tonnes of concentrate containing 17,604 tonnes of zinc metal in the June quarter, up from 25,396 tonnes of 62.3 percent zinc concentrates in the March quarter.
Full year zinc concentrate output was 107,209 tonnes grading 61.9 percent zinc while annual lead output was 25,615 tonnes of 76.8 percent concentrates.
Production came from the Cadjebut, Kapok and Goongewa mines and some Pillara ore mined during underground exploration.
